sample_unit: patient education documents (5 website sources and 3 AI-generated outputs)

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated versus website spinal fusion patient education material (FKGL, FKRE, GFI)
links.effect: Website-sourced PEM had superior readability with lower FKGL and GFI and higher FKRE than AI-generated PEM; AI PEMAT understandability/actionability was 57.6% vs 77.1% for websites (P<.001).
links.quote: Website-sourced PEM exhibited superior readability with lower FKGL and GFI scores and higher FKRE scores.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient materials measured by FKGL and Gunning Fog Index
links.effect: AI-generated PEM was less readable than institution/society PEM, with higher FKGL and GFI grade levels and lower reading ease scores.
links.quote: Website-sourced PEM exhibited superior readability with lower FKGL and GFI scores and higher FKRE scores.

links.outcome: Quality and reliability of AI-generated PEM by DISCERN and PEMAT
links.effect: Website-sourced materials scored higher on PEMAT (77.1% vs 57.6%, P<.001) and DISCERN (59.667 vs 49, P=.006) than AI-generated content.
links.quote: Website-sourced materials scored significantly higher PEMAT (77.1% ± 9.8%, vs. 57.6% ± 6.3% for AI-generated PEM (P < .001)) and DISCERN scores (59.667 ± 9.686 vs. 49 ± 4.884, P = .006).

unlisted_practices: Follow-up prompting to improve quality of AI-generated patient education material (improvement in DISCERN not statistically significant, P=.024)

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates LLMs generating patient education material compared to institutional websites, and specifically tests the effect of follow-up prompting on content quality.
